title: Multi-stage Quantum Amplifier Readout Chain
authors: Logan Howe, Andrea Giachero, Michael Vissers, Corwin Shiu, Shannon Duff, Jason Austermann, Johannes Hubmayr, Joel Ullom
abstract: Multi-stage cryogenic readout chains with a wide bandwidth and added noise within a few quanta of the quantum limit are frequently constructed using traveling-wave parametric amplifiers (TWPAs) as the first stage, and a semiconductor amplifier as the second stage. Unfortunately for highly-scaled superconducting detector arrays, or quantum information systems, and space-based observatories, the power dissipation of the semiconductor amplifier becomes problematic from the perspective of available cryogenic cooling power at \mbox{3~K to 4~K}. Here we demonstrate a readout chain based on a two-stage kinetic inductance TWPA (KTWPA). This quantum-amplifier-based-readout-chain (QARC) provides sufficient gain that a cryogenic semiconductor follow-on amplifier can be eliminated without degradation of the system noise. In this way, the QARC dissipates approximately three orders of magnitude less power than readout chains containing semiconductor amplifiers while adding noise of less than 2~quanta over a 1~GHz bandwidth. In addition, by leveraging the high power handling of kinetic inductance technology, the QARC maintains an input compression point of -93~dBm, which exceeds that of many contemporary Josephson-junction-based parametric amplifiers.
summary: The paper presents a novel Quantum-Amplifier-Based Readout Chain (QARC) that replaces power-hungry semiconductor amplifiers with cascaded Kinetic Inductance TWPAs. This design drastically reduces cryogenic power dissipation while maintaining near-quantum-limited noise performance, making large-scale quantum detector arrays more feasible for demanding environments like space applications.
main_problem: Developing low-dissipation, wide bandwidth, and near-quantum-limited readout chains for superconducting detectors where traditional semiconductor amplifiers cause excessive cryogenic power dissipation.
main_result: The proposed Quantum-Amplifier-Based Readout Chain (QARC) using two stages of Kinetic Inductance TWPAs achieves sufficient gain while dissipating three orders of magnitude less power than semiconductor-containing alternatives.
method: Experimental characterization and noise measurement comparing QARCs against semi-QARCs, utilizing various quantum noise sources like tunnel junctions and diffusive resistors.
model_or_system: The system is a multi-stage cryogenic readout chain built from Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifiers (TWPAs) based on kinetic inductance technology. It compares the performance of this pure quantum amplifier chain (QARC) against chains incorporating semiconductor amplifiers (semi-QARC).
key_observables: System excess noise ($	ext{N}_{	ext{sys,ex}}$), system gain ($	ext{G}_{	ext{sys}}$), and power dissipation.
important_parameters: Noise added must be less than 2 quanta over a 1 GHz bandwidth; QARC dissipates $\sim$ three orders of magnitude less power than HEMT chains.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that eliminating semiconductor amplifiers significantly reduces the cryogenic cooling burden, enabling scalability for large detector arrays or space applications.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematics comparing QARC and semi-QARC setups; performance plots show system excess noise ($	ext{N}_{	ext{sys,ex}}$) vs. frequency using different noise sources (SNTJ, MR); power vs. bias voltage curves validate the measurement techniques.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem of cryogenic cooling limits in large detector arrays. It then introduces and characterizes the QARC using KTWPAs, demonstrating its low dissipation and high performance compared to existing methods. Finally, it validates the noise measurements by cross-referencing multiple quantum noise sources.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum optics as it pushes the boundaries of measurement sensitivity in solid-state quantum devices by minimizing classical noise contributions from amplifiers.

Each KTWPA is individually biased and pumped for maximum tunability and both individual and in-tandem performance optimization.
